title: The State of the Collection - 2021
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vb5gSRAHXCA

A collection tour Daniel (@dungeondive) wasn't going to film, made because people asked — and the reason for the reluctance turns out to be the interesting part. Little has changed, because roughly as much left as arrived, and he wasn't won over by many new games in 2020.

What the walkthrough actually documents is triage. Some twenty games are inbound with no room for them, so the collection has to become "super curated" — only what he loves survives. Bloodborne came and is going; Dark Souls finally sold for about $20, a heavy loss he mentions without much regret. Sands of Sheerak is out after he got answers from the designer and concluded he dislikes everything it adds over Forests of Adrimon.

Two passages stand out. He is done with gamebooks — not disparagingly, but because he keeps trying to reignite an old enthusiasm and no longer needs to, keeping only his Fabled Lands. And he is done buying artistic RPG books, having realised on the Super Blood Harvest review that the only person who enjoys the artistry is the owner reading it; he wants those authors to write solo games so the buyer can actually play the book they bought.

He predicts, accurately, that he'll rewatch this and find he said he'd sell 60% of his games.

----

When shelf space runs out, is a curated collection a better collection — or just a smaller one?
